Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Eritreans 18 years and older are required to obtain a national ID card. Children under 18 born to Eritrean parents can obtain an Underage ID. Eritreans aged 18-35 without a national ID can apply for a temporary ID. This tiered system covers eligibility from childhood through adulthood. Score=3 reflecting age 18 mandatory with underage provisions.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Corroborated with three additional sources (IRB Canada 2018 report citing EASO/UK Border Agency 2012; IRB Canada RIR citing 2012 UK Border Agency testimony): Eritrea's National ID card is mandatory only from age 18, not 6-10 as coded. The original comment itself states 'age 18 mandatory' yet was scored 3 (6-10 range), an internal inconsistency with no supporting evidence found for that band. Recoded to 1 (>17) reflecting the mandatory registration age for the primary national ID credential. Note: a separate 'Underage ID' is available from birth for children of Eritrean parents, but sources describe it explicitly as a travel document issued 'in lieu of a visa' for diaspora minors visiting Eritrea, not a domestic enrolment pathway into the identity system — flagged for human review as to whether this should instead lower the eligibility age toward <1 (code 5) if considered part of the same system.
